_comment: Networking: the mini-protocol codecs and state machines (module protocol) and the bearer, multiplexer, connection manager, protocol clients and servers, and peer selection (module network). Their reference is ouroboros-network, and ouroboros-consensus for the block and transaction types the protocols carry. docs/design/correspondence-map.md says what an entry holds; scripts/check_correspondence.py checks it.

class protocol.ChainSync.Limits.note: the defaults refuse a MsgFindIntersect of more than 64 points or 8192 items; the reference reads any number of points within smallByteLimit

class protocol.KeepAlive.Cookie.note: a newtype of Word16; the Scala class holds an Int checked to that range at construction

def protocol.Handshake.acceptOrRefuse.note: greatest common version, else VersionMismatch of the local versions in ascending order; decode its data, else HandshakeDecodeError; accept it, else Refused. Failures stay typed (SelectionError) and refusal renders their text. Offers are a Vector its callers keep distinct (proposal refuses duplicates); the branch for a common version missing from the offers cannot be taken

def protocol.Handshake.message.note: the message read from the term the parser read whole, as object protocol.Handshake's entry says (#796): the key and the items checked once the term is whole, where decodeMsg checks (key, length) before reading on. Visible in the package so that the test oracle of the parser before it resumed reads its terms with it; unchanged

def protocol.Handshake.reason.note: a refusal's reason read from its term, as object protocol.Handshake's entry says (#796); visible in the package for the same test oracle; unchanged

def protocol.KeepAlive.transition.note: the reference's transitions and agency are in the message and StateAgency types; this is the same table at run time

def protocol.PeerSharingEngine.decodeTyp.note: the length of the message's array is read and ignored (a definite array whose length cborg's decodeListLen holds in an Int), then the key as a word; in StIdle 0 is MsgShareRequest with its Word8 amount and 2 is MsgDone, in StBusy 1 is MsgSharePeers with a definite or indefinite list of peers (decodeListWith), and any other key is refused. Agency, which the reference has in its state tokens, is the same table checked at run time; the byte limit its Cursor applies while reading is the driver's (runDecoderWithLimit, framework Driver/Limits.hs:295-331, with byteLimitsPeerSharing); a MsgSharePeers that arrives in parts is read on after the peers read whole (attemptTyped), as decodeMsg runs from the stream through mkCodecCborLazyBS (Codec.hs:42)

enum network.KeepAliveClient.Cookies.note: Fresh, the default, seeds each client's generator from the platform's secure generator when the client is made, an approved deviation: the reference gives the client of every connection the node's one keepAliveRng. Shared starts every client from one generator, as the reference does, for tests and tools. The generator is Scarab's Rng (SplitMix64 with a fixed gamma), not splitmix's SMGen; no peer can observe which uniform generator drew the cookies, since only the node's own client compares them, the seed is random and each cookie is a uniform Word16 (the low 16 bits of the next 64, as random's Word16 draw truncates)

enum protocol.ChainSync.Message.note: the eight messages in the reference's order, with the same fields; the header is the type parameter P, and the states they go between are checked by ChainSyncEngine.transition

enum protocol.KeepAlive.Message.note: MsgKeepAlive, MsgKeepAliveResponse and MsgDone; the states they go between are checked by transition

enum protocol.PeerSharing.Message.note: MsgShareRequest, MsgSharePeers and MsgDone; the reference's peerAddress parameter is fixed to Address, the wire form of the RemoteAddress cardano-diffusion instantiates it with

enum protocol.PeerSharing.Violation.note: PeerSharingProtocolViolation PeerSharingAmount Int; the reference throws it from peerSharingClient (PeerSharing.hs:128-130), here it is a typed value

object protocol.Handshake.note: its private parser reads a message as one generic term and checks it afterwards, where decodeMsg reads the list length and key and checks (key, length) before reading on, so a malformed message can be refused at another item and with other text (#796). As the reference since #1029: a refusal's reason is read as decodeRefuseReason reads it, its length read and ignored; generic terms and strings have no depth, count or size cap, only the message's 5760 bytes on receipt (runDecoderWithLimit); the encoder writes a message of any size, as encodeMsg does and the driver sends it (sendMessage, Driver/Limits.hs:109-117); a term keeps an indefinite string's chunks and writes them, an empty indefinite text and its simple values as cborg 0.2.10.0's encodeTerm writes them; and a simple value after 0xf8 is read whatever its value, as decodeTerm reads it. Still different, also #796: a float keeps its width and NaN payload when written, where cborg writes every NaN as f97e00 (Write.hs:580); and tags 2 and 3 are kept with any payload, where decodeTerm reads them as integers and refuses a payload that is not bytes; the parser reads a message that arrives in parts on from the head it stopped at, with the terms it has read (incremental), as decodeMsg runs from the stream through mkCodecCborLazyBS (Codec.hs:117)

object protocol.PeerSharing.note: its private address reader is decodeRemoteAddress: the address's length is read and ignored, then its tag as a word (0 or 1, any other refused), then one or four Word32 and the port as a Word16; its private writer is encodeRemoteAddress, [0, word32, port] and [1, word32 x 4, port]. The rest converts between the facade's messages and PeerSharingEngine's

object protocol.TxSubmission2.note: the node runs eraCodec, which carries the GenTx and GenTxId of every Shelley-based era under the era's index, as the reference's dispatchEncoder and dispatchDecoder do; a Byron GenTx or GenTxId is a protocol error here, where the reference decodes it and its mempool refuses it with the era mismatch. codec, Conway's alone, is the view the Message facade keeps

type protocol.PeerSharing.Values.Amount.note: a newtype of Word8; the opaque type holds an Int that its constructors keep in 0..255

val protocol.Handshake.DefaultPhaseTimeo.note: StPropose and StConfirm: shortWait, 10 seconds (node-to-node; node-to-client runs noTimeLimitsHandshake, Codec.hs:91-99)

val protocol.Handshake.MaxMessageBytes.note: StPropose and StConfirm both take maxTransmissionUnit, 4 * 1440 = 5760 bytes

val protocol.KeepAlive.CodecVersion.note: the codec in use is codecKeepAlive_v2

val protocol.KeepAlive.UpstreamMessageBy.note: both active states take smallByteLimit, 65535 bytes

val protocol.PeerSharing.UpstreamMessage.note: both active states take maxTransmissionUnit, 4 * 1440 = 5760 bytes

class protocol.TxSubmission2.EraTxId.note: the era of the NS and, in a Shelley-based era, its 32-byte id; where the reference compares ids, by the hash alone whatever the era (OneEraGenTxId's Eq and Ord, lines 167-181), the node compares the id (TxSubmission2Runtime.eraRules, the sink's known)

class protocol.TxSubmission2.EraTx.note: the era of the NS and the transaction's bytes, which the era's GenTx carries CBOR-in-CBOR

def protocol.TxSubmission2.eraCodec.note: [era, #6.24(tx)] and [era, id] of every Shelley-based era, each transaction read by the decoders of the era it names; a Byron GenTx or GenTxId, which the reference decodes, is a protocol error here

class network.DuplexPeers.note: the inbound governor State's matureDuplexPeers (a Map) and freshDuplexPeers (an OrdPSQ keyed by address, ordered by registration time), and the timing of the inbound governor's steps that drive them (inboundGovernorStep). The fresh peers are a Map of each peer's registration time and data in place of the OrdPSQ: a different internal structure with the same observable behaviour (the maturation boundary, and what a registration and an unregistration do, each mapped below as a Mirror), which following the reference does not require (decisions register, reference fidelity, 2026-10-27: following the reference means following its observable behaviour; internal algorithms may differ). Registrations come from accepted duplex connections and, while the node listens, from dialled duplex ones that this side announces (OutboundPeers, Announcement), as the connection manager announces both (Core.hs 982-995, 1594-1630); the end of an accepted connection of either data flow unregisters its address. The class is that of the steps' timing, an approved deviation (decisions register, networking, 2026-11-19): the steps run in the node, outside this map's roots (PeerSharingRuntime.maturing, InboundGovernor.run), on each registration and unregistration and on inactionTimeout, where the reference's inbound governor also steps on its connections' other events, which Scarab's handles per connection; and a registration is stamped with the time the step handles it, where the reference stamps it with its step's time read before the wait. So an address becomes mature only once some registration of it still in force was handled at least 900 s earlier, and a single unreplaced registration matures within one more inactionTimeout when the steps run promptly; the reference can mature the same address earlier or later (docs/compatibility/network-peersharing.md, Inbound peers)

def network.DuplexPeers#registered.note: the Duplex branch of NewConnection's freshDuplexPeers update: OrdPSQ.insert at the given time (the reference's step's time, read before its wait; Scarab's caller passes the time the step handles it), replacing the time of a present fresh peer, mature peers untouched. The pins differ only for a connection id already tracked (c45735a5 372-392 re-inserts; 4646039f 296-304 and 2f1c154f 297-304 keep the state and its time); Scarab registers each duplex connection once, from its own handshake, so that branch has no counterpart

def network.DuplexPeers#unregistered.note: the peer half of unregisterConnection: the remote address leaves matureDuplexPeers and freshDuplexPeers, whatever the data flow of the connection that ended (Scarab tracks accepted unidirectional connections for this); the connection half is the connection's own lifecycle

def network.DuplexPeers#maturedPeers.note: atMostView at the time less inboundMaturePeerDelay (times <= time - 900 s): the due peers as a Map, and the rest; a partition of the fresh Map, the same decision as the OrdPSQ view

def network.DuplexPeers#matured.note: the MaturedDuplexPeers event: newly mature <> mature (left-biased, so Scala's mature ++ newly), and the rest as the fresh peers

val network.DuplexPeers.InactionTimeout.note: 31.415927 seconds, exactly, at all three pins

def network.DuplexPeers.empty.note: emptyState's matureDuplexPeers = Map.empty and freshDuplexPeers = OrdPSQ.empty

enum protocol.NetworkError.RangeRefusal.note: one case for each exception the reference raises for a range, named as it is: NoGenesisBlock and BlockGCed (BlockFetchServerException), InvalidIteratorRange (ChainDbError), InvalidIteratorRangeError (the ImmutableDB's ApiMisuse); as a closed type, each ends the connection

enum network.BlockFetchServer.UnknownRan.note: MissingBlock and ForkTooOld, each with its point; the server answers either with NoBlocks

enum network.BlockFetchServer.IteratorRe.note: IteratorExhausted, IteratorResult and IteratorBlockGCed as Exhausted, Block and BlockGCed; a range's stream is the results of its iteratorNext calls up to the first Exhausted or BlockGCed

enum network.LeiosFetchJob.note: the request and its answer's continuation, a constructor per request; the continuation raises through the receiver's capability, as the reference's collector thread dies of its exception

def network.LeiosFetchPipelined.run.note: the receiver queue of the pipelined driver as a receiver fiber of its own that hands each answer on and counts it arrived; Collect (Just k) as a take of an answer that has arrived, if one has

val network.LeiosFetchPipelined.BusyTime.note: longWait, the limit of Block and BlockTxs; Idle waits forever

trait network.LeiosFetchRequestHandler.note: one method per request where the reference's is one function over the request

enum protocol.LeiosFetchRefusal.note: ExnLeiosInvalidRequest's two cases, and the throwLeiosDbException and LeiosDbException of the handler split by cause

val network.IngressLimits.LeiosNotifyByt.note: maxLeiosNotifyIngressQueue, the margin added where nodeToNode reads it

val network.IngressLimits.LeiosFetchByte.note: maxLeiosFetchIngressQueue, the margin added where nodeToNode reads it

def network.Mux.Config#sendLimit.note: LeiosFetch's messages are sent whatever their size, as muxChannel's send bounds none; the other protocols keep the node's ceiling of maxMessageBytes

enum network.HotBundle.note: withHot's two mini-protocols as the Leios build's bundle; a release build's adds none

trait network.LeiosFetchInitiator.note: the client a hot activation runs, given the stop signals its ExpandedInitiatorContext's control message gives

val network.ServerHandlers#leiosFetch.note: the handler the LeiosFetch responder answers with

enum protocol.LeiosFetchFault.note: invalidReply's errors a case each, beside ExnLeiosWellHashedBodyRejected's two; BodyNotStorable has no counterpart: unreachable, it keeps LeiosEb's construction total

def network.LeiosNotifyServer.run.note: with an empty next: each request held and counted, the client's next message read ahead, MsgQuit answered by drain's MsgCanceled for each held request and MsgDone; incr's ExcessiveRequests a typed end

def protocol.LeiosNotifyDecoder.decodeId.note: decode from StIdle, the client's messages, which carry no header

glue.reason: Scala value equality and rendering of a class with a private constructor; the reference's Cookie derives Eq and Show
construction of a Cookie inside Word16's range, the range of the reference's Cookie
Scala value equality, hashing and rendering of a class with a private constructor
Scala value equality and hashing of a class with a private constructor; the reference's Tip derives Eq
construction of a UInt64 inside the unsigned 64-bit range
the boundary scope's short-circuit, forwarded to ProtocolWire.bad and ProtocolWire.get
adapters from this facade's point, tip and payload codecs to ChainSyncEngine's codec interfaces
names under the Cardano facade for BlockFetchEngine's types, companions and values, with the point type fixed to ChainSync.Point; they decide nothing, and what they name is BlockFetchEngine's
construction of an Amount inside Word8's range, the range of the reference's PeerSharingAmount, and its getAmount accessor; trusted narrows a value the decoder has already checked against Max
Scala ordering of an Amount; the reference's PeerSharingAmount derives Ord

the unsigned words of an address on the wire: the reference takes Word32 from base and PortNumber (a Word16 on the wire, PeerSelection/PeerSharing/Codec.hs:15-19) from the network package, neither defined in ouroboros-network; these opaque types and their constructors only hold those ranges and convert from JVM integers
text of typed errors for logs, never sent on the wire; the reference's PeerSharingError derives Show
conversion between Scarab's own types: decodePrefix's Decoding as the multiplexer's ChainSync.DecodeResult

Scarab's own typed outcome of a hot peer's ChainSync session, which the node places on the governor's asynchronous demotion for its log line and its Antithesis assertions (#1032); the governor decides nothing on it
stack-safe structural equality, hashing and rendering of a generic term (codec.Tree), which nests as deep as a 5760-byte message allows; the reference's CBOR.Term derives Eq and Show
the Message facade's view of an engine message of eraCodec, in a runtime violation's report: each id and transaction without its era

the reference's credit and request rules (TxSubmissionPolicy) over era-tagged ids, comparing them by their hash as OneEraGenTxId's Eq and Ord do, a received transaction answering the request when its id is one asked for

the hook by which the node's decoder of a HasTx id judges an id that has not all arrived, and the server source's member naming it: the reference hands the codec the decoder itself (decodeTxId, LocalTxMonitor/Codec.hs:45 and 135-137 at ouroboros-network c45735a5) and reads the id from the stream; Scarab reads a whole id as one item, and the judgement is in the node, outside the areas

the hook by which the node's decoder of a GenTx judges a LocalTxSubmission transaction, whole or the part that has arrived: the reference hands the codec the decoder itself (decodeTx, LocalTxSubmission/Codec.hs:148-154 at ouroboros-network c45735a5) and reads the transaction from the stream; Scarab reads the transaction as one item and asks the node's judge of it, which is outside the areas

the query reader's judgement of a LocalStateQuery query that has not all arrived: the reference hands the codec the decoder of queries itself (decodeQuery, LocalStateQuery/Codec.hs:169-170 at ouroboros-network c45735a5) and reads the query from the stream; Scarab reads a whole query as one item, and the judgement is in the node, outside the areas
the companion of DuplexPeers, holding its constants and its empty value

the typed outcome of Connection#negotiated: whether the side that negotiated a connection announces it to the inbound governor, which the reference decides inline (ConnectionManager/Core.hs 982-989 and 1622-1630) in the code Connection#negotiated mirrors

how a decoder keeps its progress on a message not all of which has arrived, so that a longer prefix is read on from where it stopped and nothing read whole is read again: the reference keeps that progress in its decoder's continuation (cborg 0.2.10.0 deserialiseIncremental, src/Codec/CBOR/Read.hs:169-172 and 1254-1260; typed-protocols 1.2.2.0 convertCborDecoderLBS, cborg/Network/TypedProtocol/Codec/CBOR.hs:136-164), fed a chunk at a time by runDecoderWithLimit (ouroboros-network framework/lib/Ouroboros/Network/Driver/Limits.hs:281-331 at c45735a5 and 4646039f); here a decoder's cursor holds it as a value. What each codec accepts and refuses, and where, is the codec's as before; each codec's incremental is its decodePrefix as the multiplexer takes it (decodePrefix is it started afresh), the reading itself in the codec's own definitions as before
the Leios clients of the hand-run probe (LeiosProbe) read each prefix from its start: the Leios decoders keep no progress on a message not all of which has arrived; no node path uses them

the opt-in outbound limit, a Deviation the owner approved (docs/decisions.md, networking, 2026-11-18): the reference's connection manager reserves a connection without any limit (acquireOutboundConnectionImpl, ConnectionManager/Core.hs:1390-1418 at ouroboros-network c45735a5), so the limit, its positive count, the kind of dial it counts or leaves out (local roots) and the check of a limit against what the governor dials at once have no counterpart

the governor's classification of a peer for the opt-in outbound limit, read by a dial when it reserves its connection, and the step by which a connection of a peer that became a local root is left out of the limit, a Deviation the owner approved (docs/decisions.md, networking, 2026-11-18): the reference has no outbound limit, so it classifies no dial for one and a connection holds no place there to give back
the text of a BlockFetch range refusal, for presentation only; the reference shows its exceptions with derived Show instances

the LeiosFetch runtime's Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own: the client's settings record and instruction alias, the message tag a refusal names, the companions, the refusal's rendering, and the decoder the multiplexer receives a LeiosFetch message with, the codec resumed on each longer prefix from the step its last prefix stopped in, as the driver feeds cborg's decoder each chunk (#54)

the LeiosFetch codec read in steps, so that a message the driver receives in parts is read once and refused at the first token the codec refuses, as cborg's incremental decoder reads the reference's single Decoder: the checkpoints between steps and the one a message starts from, the runner that resumes from a checkpoint, and a counted collection's head and its next entry with the entries read so far (the bound checks of the reference's decodeBitmaps and of its transaction list); cborg's incremental decoding is the runtime's, with no definition to map (#54)

the Leios answers' Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own: the fault's rendering and companion, the total constructors of the wire's words, a Word32 by fromIntegral and a slot bounded into a Word64, and the hot stop a client registers so that it reads the governor's Terminate first, which the reference's client reads from controlMessageSTM in the same transaction as its next request (#54)

the LeiosNotify server's Scala plumbing with no counterpart of its own: its companion, and the decoder the multiplexer receives the client's two-byte messages with, read from the start of each longer prefix (#54)

the latch by which a hot activation's clean end stops its LeiosFetch client, standing for the Terminate of the control message the reference's client reads in STM (nextLeiosFetchClientCommand), its stop reached even when registered after it fires (#54)
construction of a Leios wire Word64 from the bits of another Word64, such as a slot; the reference's LeiosPoint holds the SlotNo itself (#73)
